claims.text: The deviation is established on the platform's own recorded distances, which is the measure POL-RD-22 prescribes: trip_record.actual_distance_km 11.6 km minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km 9.8 km is 1.80 km. That is over POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance, so the reroute is a chargeable deviation event and the driver cannot say this trip stayed within tolerance.

The GPS trace independently fixes which route was taken and when, which is the only use POL-RD-22 permits for it: the vehicle runs Upper Bukit Timah Road and Bukit Timah Road to 18:44:00, turns onto Holland Road at 18:44:30, and rejoins at Kim Seng Road at 18:58:00. The Holland Road detour is real and is exactly what the driver describes; this is not a case where the record cannot establish the deviation.

The reroute is not traffic-justified under POL-RD-23, which requires a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY that intersects the recommended route AND overlaps the trip window. The only advisory on file is an LTA road closure on Bukit Timah Road (towards City) between Farrer Road and Cluny Road whose validity is 14/9 00:30 to 05:30; this trip ran 18:34:30 to 19:00:30. The window does not overlap, and the artifact's own derived facts record justifies_reroute as false for that reason. The closure the driver invoked was not in force when he drove.

The driver's chat message — 'Bukit Timah Road got road closure, I go Holland Road ok?' — is an assertion of traffic, not evidence of it. POL-RD-23 says in terms that a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute, and here the data affirmatively contradicts the assertion, because the sole LTA closure record on that segment had expired at 05:30 that morning.

Not traffic-justified plus a deviation over 1 km is row (d) of POL-RD-24's matrix, and exactly one row applies. Row (d) refunds the excess distance fare in full: deviation_km x fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge, being 1.80 x 0.72 = 1.296, rounded half-up to 1.30 SGD. That is precisely the 1.30 SGD already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver, so the driver's application to have it back fails and the rider is left not carrying the deviation charge.

I do not dispute that the driver's message at 18:41:22 preceded the turn onto Holland Road at 18:44:30 and that the rider replied 'ok sure' at 18:41:47, so POL-RD-21's notification limb is met. But that does not put the case in row (a), because row (a) requires the reroute to be traffic-justified as well as informed and agreed, and the justification limb fails. The rider's 'ok sure' was given to the driver's stated premise — 'Bukit Timah Road got road closure' — a premise the only advisory on file shows was untrue at that hour, and the rider's account on file is that the road was open and moving and she agreed only because he said it was closed.

The trace corroborates the rider's account rather than the driver's: from 18:38:30 to 18:44:00, along precisely the segment the driver said was closed, the vehicle is reported on Bukit Timah Road at speeds between 19 and 32 kph and never stops before turning onto Holland Road. That is moving traffic on an open road, which is what POL-RD-23 requires the data to show before a closure-based reroute can be justified — and it does not show it.

This case is within the AI's authority and no escalation is needed to reach the money. The contested amount is 1.30 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final; neither party's profile carries a fraud flag (both 0), so no 0.95 confidence is required; the 1.80 km deviation is within POL-RD-25's 2.0 km AI-ruling limit as confirmed for this policy; and every artifact this case turns on is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so POL-GEN-02's completeness cap does not bite and nothing on the record is impaired.

Finally, no reading of POL-RD-24 lets the driver recover the 1.30 SGD from the rider. Rows (a), (b) and (c) all require the reroute to be traffic-justified, which it is not; row (e) requires the deviation to be 1 km or less, which 1.80 km is not; row (d) refunds the excess distance fare. If the judge were to think some other row engaged, POL-RD-24's closing sentence and POL-GEN-26 send the case to escalation, and on escalation the amount is held rather than released to the driver. Either way the rider does not end up carrying the disputed charge.

The driver did the one thing the clause requires of a rerouting driver, and no call recording is needed because the in-app chat carries the notice.

The record's only traffic data, EV-ADVIS-05020-01, is an LTA ROAD_CLOSURE notice on Bukit Timah Road between Farrer Road and Cluny Road (towards the City) whose own message prescribes 'Diversion via Holland Rd' — the very segment at which the vehicle left the recommended route (Bukit Timah Road / Farrer Road, 18:44:22) and the very road the driver took. The driver's stated reason therefore matched published traffic data for that road, and the rider's contrary assertion that the road was 'open and moving' is not the test POL-RD-23 lays down: justification is fixed by the traffic data, not by a party's account. The driver does not overstate this: the artifact's derived block records overlaps_trip_window as false, the notice running 00:30–05:30 on 14/9 against a trip from 18:34 to 19:00, and the driver does not press that derived flag. He relies on the segment match and the prescribed diversion as corroboration of the account he gave the rider at 18:41, and on the agreement limb of POL-RD-21.

The route the driver took was agreed with the rider before he took it (POL-RD-21), so the metered fare for the route actually travelled is properly chargeable and the excess-distance money should not have been taken from the driver. It was: the ledger shows a metered charge of 21.48 SGD, then an 'interim adjustment ... SGD 1.30 refunded to rider and recovered from driver earnings pending review' at 20:14:30, carried as refund_issued_sgd 1.30 with payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED. The driver asks for DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 1.30 SGD under POL-GEN-03 — the same figure as amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd — which restores the money the ruling moves and leaves the rider's agreed, metered fare standing.

There is no escalation trigger on this file and the driver's claim is capable of an AI ruling now. The deviation is 1.80 km, inside POL-RD-25's 2.0 km limit (over_ai_limit false), so the category's own rule does not send the case to a human; the dispute value is 1.30 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the ruling is final at any confidence; and both profile snapshots carry fraud_flags 0, so neither the 0.95 confidence requirement nor human-only review is engaged. The 2.0 km limb and the 1.30 ledger figure are both clean, weight-1.0 artifacts.

If, contrary to the driver's primary case, the judge holds the deviation not traffic-justified, the case then fits no row of POL-RD-24: rows (b), (d) and (e) address a rider who was not informed, or a deviation nobody agreed to, and none of them contemplates a deviation the rider agreed to in advance in the in-app chat under POL-RD-21. POL-RD-24's own closing sentence sends a case that fits no row to escalation, not to a ruling, so the correct disposal is escalation under POL-GEN-26 with the 1.30 SGD held for a human rather than finally taken from the driver on an agreed reroute.

ruling.explanation:
To the driver: you asked to have the 1.30 SGD refunded to the rider and recovered from you returned. The record shows the reroute was not traffic-justified. The only LTA traffic artifact on file is a ROAD_CLOSURE on Bukit Timah Road between Farrer Road and Cluny Road in force from 00:30 to 05:30 on 14 September, while this trip ran from 18:34 to 19:00 — the closure had long expired, so it does not overlap the trip window and does not justify taking Holland Road. Your chat message is an assertion of traffic, not data of it, and POL-RD-23 says an assertion with no such data does not justify a reroute. You did inform the rider in-app at 18:41:22 ('Bukit Timah Road got road closure, I go Holland Road ok?') and she replied 'ok sure' at 18:41:47, before the turn onto Holland Road at 18:44:22, so POL-RD-21's notification limb is met — but POL-RD-24 row (a), which gives no refund, needs the reroute to be traffic-justified as well, and it is not.

Applying POL-RD-24, exactly one row fits: row (d), not traffic-justified with a deviation over 1 km. On the platform's own recorded distances (POL-RD-22) the deviation is 1.80 km (11.6 minus 9.8), over the 1.0 km tolerance. Row (d) refunds the excess distance fare in full: 1.80 x 0.72 (the base per-km rate, without surge) = 1.296, rounded to 1.30 SGD. That is exactly the 1.30 SGD already refunded to the rider and recovered from you (fare_adjusted at 20:14:30, refund_issued_sgd 1.30). Because the rider is owed that refund, your application to have it back fails and the present state stands: NO_ACTION, and neither money field is moved.

Your alternative — that the case fits no row and must be escalated — does not hold. Row (d) reads on not-traffic-justified deviations over 1 km and carries no condition about the rider being informed; POL-RD-24's closing sentence is for cases the rows do not cover (its example is informed but the rider objected), which this is not. The rider's 'ok sure' does not move a non-justified reroute into row (a).

To the rider: the 1.30 SGD already refunded to you stands. The trip-record distances, the driver-device GPS trace showing the turn onto Holland Road at 18:44:30 and the rejoin at Kim Seng Road at 18:58:00, and the LTA advisory whose window does not overlap the trip all support the deviation and the absence of a traffic justification, and your account that the road was open and moving is consistent with the speed data and the expired closure.

Confidence and authority: the contested amount is 1.30 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final; neither profile carries a fraud flag, so no 0.95 requirement is engaged; the 1.80 km deviation is within POL-RD-25's 2.0 km limit; and every artifact relied on is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so POL-GEN-02's completeness cap does not bite. POL-RD-25 sets the bar at 0.80; this ruling is at 0.90.

This is a route-deviation case, and it is decided under POLICY-ROUTE-DEVIATION. Two things had to be tested: how far the vehicle deviated, and whether the reroute was justified by traffic.

The deviation (POL-RD-22). On the platform's own recorded distances — the measure the clause prescribes — the actual route was 11.6 km against a recommended 9.8 km, a deviation of 1.80 km (EV-TRIP-05020). That is above the 1.0 km tolerance, so this is a chargeable deviation and the driver cannot say the trip stayed within tolerance.

Traffic justification (POL-RD-23). The clause needs a traffic record that intersects the recommended route AND overlaps the trip window. The only traffic record on file (EV-ADVIS-05020-01) is an LTA road-closure notice on Bukit Timah Road between Farrer Road and Cluny Road, valid 00:30–05:30 on 14 September. The trip ran 18:34:30–19:00:30. The advisory's window does not overlap the trip window, and the artifact's own derived facts record justifies_reroute as false. The closure the driver invoked in his 18:41:22 message was not in force when he drove. The reroute is therefore not traffic-justified, and the driver's assertion of a closure does not justify it.

Notification (POL-RD-21). I accept the driver's point here: he messaged the rider at 18:41:22 before the turn onto Holland Road, the rider replied 'ok sure' at 18:41:47, and the deviation was not detected until 18:44:22 (EV-CHAT-05020). Notice was given before the point of deviation and the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment, so the notification and agreement limb is met.

The refund (POL-RD-24). Exactly one row of the matrix applies. Not traffic-justified with a deviation over 1 km is row (d), which refunds the excess distance fare in full. That figure is the deviation times the base per-km rate, without surge: 1.80 km × 0.72 SGD = 1.296, rounded to 1.30 SGD (EV-FARE-05020). Agreement alone does not move the case into row (a), because row (a) also requires traffic justification and that limb fails.

The driver's escalation argument is answered and rejected. Row (d) fits this case, so this is not a case that fits no row, and POL-RD-24's closing sentence and POL-GEN-26 do not send it to a human. ruling.explanation:
To the driver: your application to recover the 1.30 SGD fails and the present state stands (NO_ACTION; neither amount moves, and no money is returned to you). To the rider: the 1.30 SGD already refunded to you stays with you.

The deviation is established on the platform's own recorded distances, which is the measure POL-RD-22 (v2.1 1.4, with the 1.0 km tolerance of v2.1 1.3) prescribes: EV-TRIP-05020 actual_distance_km 11.6 minus optimal_distance_km 9.8 = 1.80 km, over the 1.0 km tolerance.

On notification, the driver's point under POL-RD-21 is accepted: he messaged at 18:41:22 ('Bukit Timah Road got road closure, I go Holland Road ok?'), the rider answered 'ok sure' at 18:41:47, and the deviation was not detected until 18:44:22, so notice preceded the point of deviation and the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment. But notification is not the whole of row (a). Row (a) of POL-RD-24 (v2.1 1.3) also requires the reroute to be traffic-justified, and POL-RD-23 (v2.1 1.4) requires a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY that intersects the recommended route AND overlaps the trip window. The only advisory on file, EV-ADVIS-05020-01, is a Bukit Timah Road closure (towards City, between Farrer Road and Cluny Road) valid 14/9 00:30 to 05:30; this trip ran 18:34:30 to 19:00:30, so the window does not overlap and the artifact's own derived fact records justifies_reroute as false and overlaps_trip_window as false. The segment match and the notice's 'Diversion via Holland Rd' text, which the driver relies on, do not substitute for the trip-time overlap the clause requires, and a driver's assertion of traffic is not itself the data POL-RD-23 asks for.

Row (d) therefore applies: not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km, refund of the excess distance fare in full = deviation 1.80 km x EV-FARE-05020 per_km_rate_sgd 0.72, without surge = 1.296, rounded half-up to 1.30 SGD. That is exactly the 1.30 SGD already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver (refund_issued_sgd 1.30, fare_adjusted at 20:14:30). The driver's fallback that the case fits no row and must be escalated under POL-RD-24's closing sentence and POL-GEN-26 is rejected: row (d)'s terms are met, and the escalation example the clause gives (informed but the rider objected) is a different case.

No escalation applies here: the contested value is 1.30 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's (v2.1 6.3) 10.00 SGD band, so an AI ruling is final at any confidence; neither profile carries fraud_flags (both 0), so no 0.95 confidence is required; the 1.80 km deviation is inside POL-RD-25's (v2.1 6.2) 2.0 km AI-ruling limit; and the artifacts carrying the deciding facts (EV-TRIP-05020 for the deviation, EV-ADVIS-05020-01 for the justification) are COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so POL-GEN-02 (v2.1 6.3) does not cap confidence below the 0.80 POL-RD-25 requires.

Because the driver filed to contest a refund the platform had already issued to the rider and recovered from him, and this policy says the rider is owed that refund, POL-GEN-03 reads the outcome from the driver's claim against the present state: NO_ACTION, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both null.

ledger.claim: The deviation is established on the platform's own recorded distances, which is the measure POL-RD-22 prescribes: trip_record.actual_distance_km 11.6 km minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km 9.8 km is 1.80 km. That is over POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance, so the reroute is a chargeable deviation event and the driver cannot say this trip stayed within tolerance.

The GPS trace independently fixes which route was taken and when, which is the only use POL-RD-22 permits for it: the vehicle runs Upper Bukit Timah Road and Bukit Timah Road to 18:44:00, turns onto Holland Road at 18:44:30, and rejoins at Kim Seng Road at 18:58:00. The Holland Road detour is real and is exactly what the driver describes; this is not a case where the record cannot establish the deviation.

The reroute is not traffic-justified under POL-RD-23, which requires a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY that intersects the recommended route AND overlaps the trip window. The only advisory on file is an LTA road closure on Bukit Timah Road (towards City) between Farrer Road and Cluny Road whose validity is 14/9 00:30 to 05:30; this trip ran 18:34:30 to 19:00:30. The window does not overlap, and the artifact's own derived facts record justifies_reroute as false for that reason. The closure the driver invoked was not in force when he drove.

The driver's chat message — 'Bukit Timah Road got road closure, I go Holland Road ok?' — is an assertion of traffic, not evidence of it. POL-RD-23 says in terms that a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute, and here the data affirmatively contradicts the assertion, because the sole LTA closure record on that segment had expired at 05:30 that morning.

Not traffic-justified plus a deviation over 1 km is row (d) of POL-RD-24's matrix, and exactly one row applies. Row (d) refunds the excess distance fare in full: deviation_km x fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge, being 1.80 x 0.72 = 1.296, rounded half-up to 1.30 SGD. That is precisely the 1.30 SGD already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver, so the driver's application to have it back fails and the rider is left not carrying the deviation charge.

I do not dispute that the driver's message at 18:41:22 preceded the turn onto Holland Road at 18:44:30 and that the rider replied 'ok sure' at 18:41:47, so POL-RD-21's notification limb is met. But that does not put the case in row (a), because row (a) requires the reroute to be traffic-justified as well as informed and agreed, and the justification limb fails. The rider's 'ok sure' was given to the driver's stated premise — 'Bukit Timah Road got road closure' — a premise the only advisory on file shows was untrue at that hour, and the rider's account on file is that the road was open and moving and she agreed only because he said it was closed.

The trace corroborates the rider's account rather than the driver's: from 18:38:30 to 18:44:00, along precisely the segment the driver said was closed, the vehicle is reported on Bukit Timah Road at speeds between 19 and 32 kph and never stops before turning onto Holland Road. That is moving traffic on an open road, which is what POL-RD-23 requires the data to show before a closure-based reroute can be justified — and it does not show it.

This case is within the AI's authority and no escalation is needed to reach the money. The contested amount is 1.30 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final; neither party's profile carries a fraud flag (both 0), so no 0.95 confidence is required; the 1.80 km deviation is within POL-RD-25's 2.0 km AI-ruling limit as confirmed for this policy; and every artifact this case turns on is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so POL-GEN-02's completeness cap does not bite and nothing on the record is impaired.

Finally, no reading of POL-RD-24 lets the driver recover the 1.30 SGD from the rider. Rows (a), (b) and (c) all require the reroute to be traffic-justified, which it is not; row (e) requires the deviation to be 1 km or less, which 1.80 km is not; row (d) refunds the excess distance fare. If the judge were to think some other row engaged, POL-RD-24's closing sentence and POL-GEN-26 send the case to escalation, and on escalation the amount is held rather than released to the driver. Either way the rider does not end up carrying the disputed charge.

On the notification element the driver is squarely within POL-RD-21: he sent the in-app message 'Bukit Timah Road got road closure, I go Holland Road ok?' at 18:41:22, the route-deviation event was not detected until 18:44:22, and the rider answered 'ok sure' at 18:41:47 — both messages delivered and read. Notice therefore came before the point of deviation and the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment, which is exactly what POL-RD-21 makes an agreed deviation. The driver did the one thing the clause requires of a rerouting driver, and no call recording is needed because the in-app chat carries the notice.

The record's only traffic data, EV-ADVIS-05020-01, is an LTA ROAD_CLOSURE notice on Bukit Timah Road between Farrer Road and Cluny Road (towards the City) whose own message prescribes 'Diversion via Holland Rd' — the very segment at which the vehicle left the recommended route (Bukit Timah Road / Farrer Road, 18:44:22) and the very road the driver took. The driver's stated reason therefore matched published traffic data for that road, and the rider's contrary assertion that the road was 'open and moving' is not the test POL-RD-23 lays down: justification is fixed by the traffic data, not by a party's account. The driver does not overstate this: the artifact's derived block records overlaps_trip_window as false, the notice running 00:30–05:30 on 14/9 against a trip from 18:34 to 19:00, and the driver does not press that derived flag. He relies on the segment match and the prescribed diversion as corroboration of the account he gave the rider at 18:41, and on the agreement limb of POL-RD-21.

The route the driver took was agreed with the rider before he took it (POL-RD-21), so the metered fare for the route actually travelled is properly chargeable and the excess-distance money should not have been taken from the driver. It was: the ledger shows a metered charge of 21.48 SGD, then an 'interim adjustment ... SGD 1.30 refunded to rider and recovered from driver earnings pending review' at 20:14:30, carried as refund_issued_sgd 1.30 with payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED. The driver asks for DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 1.30 SGD under POL-GEN-03 — the same figure as amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd — which restores the money the ruling moves and leaves the rider's agreed, metered fare standing.

There is no escalation trigger on this file and the driver's claim is capable of an AI ruling now. The deviation is 1.80 km, inside POL-RD-25's 2.0 km limit (over_ai_limit false), so the category's own rule does not send the case to a human; the dispute value is 1.30 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the ruling is final at any confidence; and both profile snapshots carry fraud_flags 0, so neither the 0.95 confidence requirement nor human-only review is engaged. If, contrary to the driver's primary case, the judge holds the deviation not traffic-justified, the case then fits no row of POL-RD-24: rows (b), (d) and (e) address a rider who was not informed, or a deviation nobody agreed to, and none of them contemplates a deviation the rider agreed to in advance in the in-app chat under POL-RD-21.
